# frimpomaasync.com

frimpomaasync.com builds practical business systems for owner-run service businesses. SynKasa handles the front desk. Siesie handles the repeating work behind it. Every build lives in the client's accounts and stays theirs.

There is a second audience with its own product. Soft Appeals recovers denied insurance claims for healthcare organizations. It adds focused recovery capacity for denied claims alongside an organization's existing billing operation, rather than replacing any part of it.

Primary slogan: "Watch it work before you pay."

Guarantee: "Live in 7 days, or you don't pay."

The guarantee covers the agreed system going live. It never promises a number of bookings, because bookings depend on the inquiries the business receives.

## Visitor path

1. Name the business leak on the homepage.
2. Take one same-day fix.
3. Watch the relevant working build.
4. Use the SynKasa fit form or Siesie application.
5. Book the confirmed 15-minute call.
6. Receive a recommendation.
7. Review the proposal and agreement.
8. Pay before onboarding begins.
9. Complete onboarding, build, testing, and approval.
10. Launch, train, and hand over.
11. Follow up on performance.
12. Request approved proof, a referral, care, or the next useful system.

The local leak finder, calculator, and Siesie check do not store or transmit visitor inputs.

## SynKasa

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/synkasa

Fit form: https://frimpomaasync.com/synkasa-fit

SynKasa is the flagship front desk, formerly sold as the Client Catcher. It answers calls, texts, and direct messages in the owner's voice, qualifies the inquiry, books the right time, and follows up.

Current tiers:

- Start: $555 once. Calls, texts, and direct messages are answered, qualified, and booked. Optional care is $99 a month.
- Grow: $1,500 once. Adds follow-up, reminders, review requests, quote chasing, and one dashboard. Optional care is $222 a month. Most owners start here.
- Full: $2,222 once. Adds proposals, deposit collection, and every customer channel the business uses. Optional care is $444 a month.
- Founding Grow: $750 for the first three owners, with a named testimonial required after the front desk has been running.

Care is optional. The front desk stays in the client's accounts if care ends. A later tier can be added to the existing build.

Soma is part of SynKasa. It carries one customer entry into the CRM, calendar, text thread, and working list.

The SynKasa fit form asks for contact details, business type, contact channels, weekly inquiry volume, current booking method, main problem, desired result, and implementation timing. A website or social page is optional.

## Siesie

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/siesie

Application: https://frimpomaasync.com/siesie-application

Siesie is the back office above the SynKasa ladder. It covers five roles:

1. Scheduling
2. Money
3. Coordination
4. Account management
5. Reporting

Siesie is $25,000 once. It is for an established business where four or five of those roles still return to the owner.

Before a Siesie build there is a paid diagnostic, the Operations Map: https://frimpomaasync.com/operations-map

The Operations Map is $2,500 and takes two weeks. It is credited in full against a Siesie build. It delivers six documents: the current-state map, the owner-dependency register, the cost of waiting, the future-state map, the sequenced and priced build plan, and a ninety-minute walkthrough. It costs the owner under four hours of their own time. If the map concludes a Siesie build is not right for the business, the fee is refunded and the owner keeps all six documents.

The representative path is: work received, scheduled, coordinated, invoiced, and reported.

The implementation path is: map, build, test, approve, launch, train, and hand over.

The owner supplies the current process, working rules, account access, and timely approvals. Judgment calls, exceptions, approvals, and sensitive conversations stay human.

The Siesie application asks for contact details, business type, team size, monthly job or client volume, current scheduling and invoicing processes, people being coordinated, owner-dependent work, the main bottleneck, implementation timing, and investment readiness. Website, current tools, and additional context are optional.

## Soft Appeals

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals

Sample Denial Recovery Assessment: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-audit

Data and security practices: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-data-security

How it works, the full recovery process: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-process

Pricing and engagement terms: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-pricing

About Soft Appeals: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-about

Start your denial review, the intake page: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-start . This is the conversion page and the first step of the service. It carries a PHI-free intake form asking only business-level questions: organization name, contact, role, organization type, unresolved denial volume, denied reimbursement range, payer names, denial types, how denials are handled today, what usually happens to unresolved denials, denial age, whether any claims are time-sensitive, and what would make the review useful. The form has no upload field and asks for no patient information by design. The sequence is: tell us about the denial situation with no PHI, Soft Appeals confirms fit, the applicable Business Associate Agreement and secure intake process are established, the 20 denials are provided securely, then the Denial Recovery Assessment is returned and the organization decides what happens next. Booking a call is not required to begin.

Frequently asked questions: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-faq . Seventy-four answers written for a vendor evaluation, grouped into starting with the service, claims and denials, working with an existing billing team, information and documentation, PHI and security, AI and technology, approval and submission, tracking, timing, pricing, scope and responsibility, fit, and what to do before sending anything. It states that appeal deadlines and appeal pathways vary by payer, plan, program and claim circumstance rather than following one universal rule, that a Business Associate Agreement is executed before PHI is exchanged where the engagement requires one, that technology assists administrative work but does not decide whether a claim is appealed, and that nothing is submitted in a client's name without client approval.

Free denial decoder: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-decoder . Type any denial reason code (like CO-16, CO-29, CO-50, CO-197, PR-204) and get the plain-English meaning, whether it points to a correction, an appeal or no further recovery effort, published context, the recommended next step, and a sample appeal-letter opening. Runs entirely in the browser and asks for no patient information. Also carries a Maryland payer-by-payer appeal deadline table.

Soft Appeals is a denied-claim revenue recovery service for healthcare organizations. It adds focused recovery capacity alongside an organization's existing billing operation rather than replacing it. Maryland first. It is a separate audience from SynKasa and Siesie and does not serve local service businesses.

Who it works with: behavioral health and therapy practices, physical and occupational therapy organizations, dental practices and groups, chiropractic and podiatry organizations, primary and specialty care organizations, multi-provider groups, and other provider organizations with unresolved claim denials. Fit depends on claim type, payer mix, denial volume, documentation available, and the scope of recovery work requested. Substance use disorder claims are out of scope.

How it works: the applicable Business Associate Agreement is executed before protected health information is exchanged. The organization sends 20 recent denied claims through the agreed secure process. Routine EHR access is not required for the initial review. Soft Appeals returns a Denial Recovery Assessment that sorts every reviewed claim by recommended action (correct or resubmit, appeal, investigate further, close or deprioritize), assigns a Recovery Priority of A, B, C or D, records the reasoning behind each recommendation, flags known time-sensitive items, and lists what each side must do next. Claims selected for recovery then move through payer-requirement research, evidence organization, appeal preparation, client approval, submission with recorded delivery evidence, follow-up tracking, and reconciliation against the payer's remittance. The workflow runs in three phases, decide then recover then resolve, across seventeen documented steps. There is no single appeal ladder applied to every claim: the pathway is determined per claim from the payer, plan, denial type and circumstances, and escalation after a second denial is a decision rather than an automatic next rung. Nothing is submitted in the organization's name without its approval.

Technology use: technology assists with organizing claim information, researching payer requirements, managing workflow, identifying follow-up items, preparing draft appeal materials, and tracking recovery activity. It does not independently authorize an appeal, make a clinical determination, change coding, or submit a claim in a client's name. Protected health information is not intentionally entered into consumer-facing AI accounts or unapproved tools, and client PHI is not intentionally used to train public or general-purpose AI models.

Fee: 25 percent of verified recovered reimbursement attributable to the recovery engagement, for eligible commercial claims accepted for recovery. The payer pays the organization directly and Soft Appeals never takes custody of payer funds. The invoice follows verification against the applicable remittance documentation. Individual claims from $150, with smaller claims worked in batches where the payer's process allows it. If no eligible recovery is achieved, no contingency fee is due for that claim. There is no setup fee, no monthly retainer and no minimum. Government-program claims may be subject to different legal, contractual or fee requirements, and their pricing and scope are agreed separately before any work begins on them. A verified recovery means payer reimbursement received by the client after authorized recovery work begins on the assigned claim and reasonably attributable to that work, verified against remittance or payment documentation. A submitted appeal does not trigger a fee, and neither does a favourable payer letter without verified reimbursement. Payment received before the engagement began, unrelated reimbursement, patient payments, duplicate or erroneous payments, and claims never accepted into the engagement are excluded. Partial recoveries are charged on the amount actually recovered, never on the amount originally denied.

The complimentary review is free of charge and the assessment belongs to the organization whether or not it continues with recovery services.

Privacy commitments: agreement before PHI, a minimum-necessary approach to information requests, no routine EHR access for the initial review, a defined technology workflow, client approval before any payer submission, and a documented data-disposition process at the end of an engagement. Where a third-party service creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI as part of the workflow, it is evaluated for its role and handled under the contractual and security requirements applicable to that relationship. Where PHI is required to be returned or destroyed at termination, it is, where feasible.

Soft Appeals makes no promise about recovery amounts or overturn rates for any organization. The statistics published on its pages are industry figures with named sources, not predictions. A recommendation to pursue a claim does not guarantee reimbursement or reversal of a payer determination.

Founder: NaNa Frimpomaa, MHA. Background in healthcare operations, performance improvement, data and administrative workflow, and health-system technology implementation including Epic go-live work. Soft Appeals is founder-led, and the founder remains accountable for work performed within the Soft Appeals scope. Soft Appeals does not make clinical, coding or legal determinations outside the agreed scope of service.

## The method

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/method

Every engagement runs the same twelve steps: useful diagnosis, fit form, 15-minute call, recommendation, proposal and agreement, payment, onboarding, build and test, approval, launch and training, follow-up, and proof, referral, or care.

Inside the build there are seven phases, each producing a document the client keeps: map, build, test, approve, launch, train, and hand over. The seven documents are the Operations Map, the build shown as it stands up, the Test Record, written approvals, the Launch Log, the Operating Manual, and the Ownership Pack.

The testing standard is published in full on that page. Six checks must pass before launch: the normal path, the exception path, the failure path, the follow-up path, the data, and ownership. If a check cannot be ticked, the build does not launch and the date moves.

## About

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/about

frimpomaasync is one person, NaNa Frimpomaa. Background: hospital front desk and patient check-in, human resources, building hospital forms, performance improvement for a healthcare system, and SQL, data management and Epic go-lives. Weekday response inside four hours, a written update every Friday, two builds at a time, no subscription to frimpomaasync.

The page also lists what is not taken on: guaranteed bookings, websites, ads, ongoing content, answering customers on the owner's behalf, selling a larger build than needed, and automating a process nobody has written down.

## Your data during a build

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/data

Covers a client engagement, not website visitors. Nothing is copied to a system frimpomaasync controls, and no database of the client's customers is held. Access is granted by the client to their own accounts, named in the scope, used only to configure, test and document, listed at handover, and revoked by the client. The page lists what each of the five Siesie roles touches and never touches. Card numbers, bank credentials and the client's money are never touched. Engagement records are kept for seven years; exports of client data are not retained. Anything held is deleted within 30 days on request. Unauthorised access is reported in writing within 72 hours.

## Privacy

Policy: https://frimpomaasync.com/privacy

Qualification forms collect only the business context a visitor chooses to submit. Public forms do not ask for passwords, payment details, customer records, private files, or account access.

Form submissions may include business type, inquiry or job volume, current process, desired result, timing, and investment readiness. They are used to review fit and prepare for the call.

Client systems are built in client-owned accounts. The signed agreement names every provider that handles client or customer data.

## Retired routes

The Client Catcher name is retired except for the "formerly" note. `/client-catcher`, `/services`, `/products`, `/solo-business-system`, and `/ai-products` redirect to `/synkasa`. `/soma` redirects to `/synkasa#soma`.
